hold_text: R12 bars a LANDING_MACHINERY diff from self-landing, and .github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml is one of its 12 entries (verified against origin/main). This declares hold and routes to the manager rather than attempting to defeat that refusal -- the refusal is the machinery protecting itself, and arming here would be the unreviewed self-landing of the very action that performs every automated landing in this repo. NEEDS A HUMAN MERGE CLICK. WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK FIRST: the input defaults to empty, so all 12 other callers are byte-for-byte unchanged -- a test pins that. The only behavioural change reaches a caller that passes refresh-command, and exactly one does (constraint-readout.yml). AND WHAT THIS CANNOT PROVE: CI does not run constraint-readout.yml, so a green here says nothing about the scheduled run. The row's criterion is an OBSERVED event=schedule run concluding success with CONSTRAINT.json on main carrying that run's generated_at -- which is why the row is NOT closed by this PR.
why: MI-280, an INSERTED unit taken from the U9 reproduction's own 'what would fix it, PROPOSED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT HERE'. It answers BL-20260911-THE-CONSTRAINT-READOUT-CRON-NOW-CLEARS-ITS-SELF-TEST-AND-DIES-ON-SESSION-BRIEF-GUARD-REJECTING-THE-BRIEF-IT-JUST-RENDERED, whose resolution_criteria demand the cause be REPRODUCED BEFORE it is fixed. It was, in #11901: cause (i) a renderer/guard disagreement REFUTED (both exit 0 on an unmoved base); cause (ii) the brief going stale against a moving base REPRODUCED with the workflow's exact verdict, introduced_registers_changed. THE DEFECT: commit-to-main's stale-branch refresh merges main in, which mints a new sha and re-triggers the checks -- and that is ALL it does. It never regenerates the derived file, so the new head carries the same stale content and the same guard fails one sha later. For a producer whose output is DERIVED FROM the registers it merges, re-running the checks is not the remedy; re-deriving is. constraint-readout.yml has concluded success ZERO times in its entire life. THE CHANGE: a new optional `refresh-command` input, empty by default so every existing caller is byte-for-byte unchanged, run after the merge and before the push. Four outcomes, never collapsed: refreshed / refreshed_rederived / refreshed_rederive_noop / failed_refresh_command -- because 'we re-derived', 'it was already correct' and 'we tried and could not' are three different facts about the head about to be pushed, and a failure pushes anyway (a strand is worse) but says so LOUDLY. Scoped to the caller's own ${PATHS}, so a re-derive can never widen what a caller lands; anything it touches outside them is REPORTED rather than silently dropped. THE TESTS RUN THE ACTION'S REAL SHELL against a real git repo, extracted verbatim from action.yml, with a test asserting the extraction still finds it -- a YAML grep for `refresh-command` would pass on a step that never executes, which is the presence-only failure new-table-wiring-guard already cost this repo. 11 assertions; 9 planted defects, 9 caught, positive control quiet. TWO APPARENT ESCAPES WERE MY OWN HARNESS'S SHELL-ESCAPING BUG, not escapes: re-planted from a file with the pattern count ASSERTED, both caught. AND THE TEST FOUND A REAL GAP IN MY OWN IMPLEMENTATION: the out-of-scope check used `git diff`, which does not see an UNTRACKED file -- so a re-derive that CREATES a file reported a clean tree for exactly the case most worth reporting. Now `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`.
